available_in718_150_1200.sourceAgreementNote: Not conservative against measurement, even in the source's own weld regime: D97 Fig. 9b (measured vs calculated gamma/Laves) shows several alloys with measured gamma/Laves above the calculated value, including alloys for which the model predicts no gamma/Laves (measured about 0.5-1.5 vol%, e.g. Ni-base alloy 8 in Fig. 3), and low-C Ni-base alloys where the model is about 2-3x high (alloys 5 and 7: measured about 2-3 vol% in Fig. 3). available_in718_150_1200.upperBoundNote: Upper bound with respect to effects that are not modelled and that all reduce segregation: solid-state back-diffusion of Nb, solute trapping at high solidification rate and dendrite-tip undercooling. comparison.note: Non-discriminating. The only quantitative as-built Nb data (Z18 EDS, 2 um probe) average over cells about 1 um wide, so they bound the cell-scale profile only loosely: both the equilibrium k (0.51) and the k(V) range give a core ratio below the lowest measured ratio, as they must if the probe averages, and neither can be confirmed or ruled out by it. No as-built study reports a Laves or NbC fraction: XRD shows FCC only (Z18, L17, K17) without a stated detection limit, and K17 sees unindexed 50-200 nm precipitates at cell boundaries. The computed terminal fractions (a few vol% at equilibrium k, less with k(V)) are therefore not tested by these observations.

in625_available.upperBoundNote: Upper bound with respect to effects that are not modelled and that all reduce the terminal constituent: solid-state back-diffusion of Nb, solute trapping at high solidification rate, dendrite-tip undercooling, and Nb tied up as NbC by carbon (no carbon model for alloy 625). It is not a bound with respect to k_Nb or C_e. Against the C88 low-Fe measurements the estimate is high (see sourceAgreementNote), but that is one set of four heats at DTA cooling, not a guarantee.

validity.ceTransferNote: C_e = 18.9 wt% Nb is not measured on alloy 625: D96 (Section IV-C) builds it from Alloy 718 data (gamma 9.3 wt% Nb in the gamma/Laves eutectic, Table V) and the Fe-diluted overlay Laves (22.1 wt% Nb, Table III). C88 gives no eutectic composition; its Laves in low-Fe alloy 625 holds less Nb (16.8-19.2 wt%, Table V), so C_e for low-Fe IN625 may be lower, which would raise the computed fraction.
validity.d96SourceNote: D96 is a single Fe-diluted (28.14 wt% Fe) GMAW overlay (Table II); wrought and LPBF IN625 (Fe <= 5 wt%) are outside it, so its k_Nb is used only as a cross-check.
validity.kTransferNote: k_Nb = 0.51 is the lowest of the four EPMA dendrite-core values in C88 Table VIII (0.51-0.53, alloys 5-8, Nb 3.53-3.61 wt%, Fe about 2.3 wt%); C88 Table VII gives 0.54 from liquidus/solidus slopes. The source Nb is 3.53-3.61 wt%, so the band ends (3.15 and 4.15 wt%) assume a constant k.

validity.outsideSourceRegimeReason: LPBF is not among the source processes (C88: GTA welds and DTA samples; D96: one GMAW overlay); k_Nb and the Scheil assumption were not established at LPBF solidification rates
validity.phaseIdentityNote: Phase identity not established. In low-Fe alloy 625 (Fe about 2.3 wt%) C88 found the terminal constituent to depend on C and Si: with 0.038 wt% C and no added Si only gamma/NbC formed (alloy 6, no Laves); with low C and no added Si a small amount of mostly Laves formed (alloy 5); Si (0.38-0.46 wt%) promoted Laves and, at low C, M6C (Sections III-B and IV-B, Tables IV and IX). D96 adds that Fe favours Laves over NbC (Section IV-B). The IN625 specification allows C up to 0.10 and Si up to 0.50 wt%, so the computed number is a gamma/Laves-type estimate with C_e = 18.9 wt% Nb, not a Laves prediction; the constituent may be gamma/NbC, gamma/Laves or both.
validity.sourceRegime: gas tungsten arc (GTA) welds and DTA samples (20 degC/min) of vacuum-melted experimental alloy 625 heats with Fe about 2.3 wt% (C88 Section II)

in718_degenerate_floor_synthetic.riskClassRule: gamma/Laves constituent > 0 at any band point under the Scheil-type model; no fitted threshold. segregation.note: When the remaining liquid at fs is below the eutectic fraction the liquid has reached the gamma/Laves composition and the ratio is capped there (atEutecticComposition = true).

source.note: full text (journal article) read for this module; Table 2 gives the solidification constants used here. Its Section 3.2 (negligible Nb diffusion / infinitely fast C diffusion, Eqs. 13-21) is the same model as the equations implemented here (D97 Eqs. 1-8)

in718_degenerate_floor_synthetic.sourceAgreementNote: Not conservative against measurement, even in the source's own weld regime: D97 Fig. 9b (measured vs calculated gamma/Laves) shows several alloys with measured gamma/Laves above the calculated value, including alloys for which the model predicts no gamma/Laves (measured about 0.5-1.5 vol%, e.g. Ni-base alloy 8 in Fig. 3), and low-C Ni-base alloys where the model is about 2-3x high (alloys 5 and 7: measured about 2-3 vol% in Fig. 3). D97 also reports that Fe and Si raise the gamma/Laves amount; IN718 contains about 18 wt% Fe plus Mo, which the source alloys do not.
in718_degenerate_floor_synthetic.upperBoundNote: Upper bound with respect to effects that are not modelled and that all reduce segregation: solid-state back-diffusion of Nb, solute trapping at high solidification rate and dendrite-tip undercooling. It is not a bound with respect to the choice of k_Nb (see validity), and it is not an upper bound on measured Laves content (see sourceAgreementNote).

validity.kTransferNote: D98 reports k_Nb = 0.45 for its Ni base alloys (Fe about 11 wt%) and 0.25 for its Fe base alloys (Fe about 45 wt%) and attributes the drop to Fe. The source gives no k_Nb(Fe) relation here, so no interpolation is made; the Fe-base result is shown as a bracketing sensitivity.

rapidSolidification.kTransferNote: V_D was fitted with k_e = 0.48 (G17, G18); this module applies it with its own equilibrium k_Nb (D98 0.45 for IN718, C88 0.51 for IN625). No source gives V_D for these k_e or for multicomponent IN718/IN625.

in718_unavailable_keyhole_leg_285_960.riskClassRule: gamma/Laves constituent > 0 at any band point under the Scheil-type model; no fitted threshold. Binary Scheil without back-diffusion predicts a terminal gamma/Laves eutectic for any Nb > 0, so this class is positive by construction for every Nb-bearing composition and does not discriminate between compositions.

segregation.note: When the remaining liquid at fs is below the eutectic fraction the liquid has reached the gamma/Laves composition and the ratio is capped there (atEutecticComposition = true).

source.citation: J.N. DuPont, C.V. Robino, A.R. Marder, 'Modeling solute redistribution and microstructural development in fusion welds of Nb-bearing superalloys', Acta Materialia 46 (1998) 4781-4790, doi:10.1016/S1359-6454(98)00123-2
source.note: full text (journal article) read for this module; Table 2 gives the solidification constants used here. Its Section 3.2 (negligible Nb diffusion / infinitely fast C diffusion, Eqs. 13-21) is the same model as the equations implemented here (D97 Eqs. 1-8)

in718_unavailable_keyhole_leg_285_960.sourceAgreementNote: Not conservative against measurement, even in the source's own weld regime: D97 Fig. 9b (measured vs calculated gamma/Laves) shows several alloys with measured gamma/Laves above the calculated value, including alloys for which the model predicts no gamma/Laves (measured about 0.5-1.5 vol%, e.g. Ni-base alloy 8 in Fig. 3), and low-C Ni-base alloys where the model is about 2-3x high (alloys 5 and 7: measured about 2-3 vol% in Fig. 3). D97 also reports that Fe and Si raise the gamma/Laves amount; IN718 contains about 18 wt% Fe plus Mo, which the source alloys do not.
in718_unavailable_keyhole_leg_285_960.upperBoundNote: Upper bound with respect to effects that are not modelled and that all reduce segregation: solid-state back-diffusion of Nb, solute trapping at high solidification rate and dendrite-tip undercooling. It is not a bound with respect to the choice of k_Nb (see validity), and it is not an upper bound on measured Laves content (see sourceAgreementNote).

validity.kTransferNote: D98 reports k_Nb = 0.45 for its Ni base alloys (Fe about 11 wt%) and 0.25 for its Fe base alloys (Fe about 45 wt%) and attributes the drop to Fe. The source gives no k_Nb(Fe) relation here, so no interpolation is made; the Fe-base result is shown as a bracketing sensitivity.
